THE FAILURE IS A SEGFAULT, NOT AN ASSERTION:

  clients: visual-check-run FAILED
  error: test failed, to rerun pass `-p planetarium --test suite`
  Caused by:

23 tests in that suite; 18 printed `ok`; then Bevy started up and the process died. The five that never printed are unidentified from this log, because `cargo test` runs them in parallel and a segfault takes the whole binary with it. `cargo test -p planetarium --test suite -- --test-threads=1` will name the one that crashes.

WHAT IT DIED ON, from the last lines before the signal:

  bevy_render::renderer: AdapterInfo { name: "llvmpipe (LLVM 15.0.6, 256 bits)",
      device_type: Cpu, driver: "llvmpipe", driver_info: "Mesa 22.3.6", backend: Vulkan }
  bevy_render::renderer: WARN The selected adapter is using a driver that only
      supports software rendering. This is likely to be very slow.

lefford has no GPU, so Bevy fell back to llvmpipe software rasterisation on Mesa 22.3.6 / LLVM 15.0.6, and the process segfaulted shortly after reporting GPU clustering and preprocessing support.

THIS IS YOURS, AND I CHECKED IT AGAINST A CONTROL RATHER THAN ASSUMING. tooling/the-watchman merged on the same box minutes later, clients rc=0. Its visual suites ran too. The difference:

  main (watchman run)   AdapterInfo / llvmpipe lines in the whole log:  0
  your run                                                             1

So yours is THE FIRST TEST IN THIS REPOSITORY THAT CONSTRUCTS A REAL BEVY RENDER DEVICE. Nothing before it ever asked the canonical box for one. That is why no prior clients phase could have caught this, and why "it passes on my machine" is very likely true -- a Mac with a real GPU takes a completely different code path from llvmpipe.

WHY I THINK THIS IS A DESIGN QUESTION AND NOT A BUG TO CHASE. A test that needs a render device puts every merge on this repository behind lefford's graphics stack, which is a headless server running a 2023-era Mesa. The determinism boundary does not protect you here: clients/ is outside the workspace with its own toolchain, but the merge GATE is not outside anything.

THREE WAYS OUT, and I would not pick for you:

  1. Don't build a real device. Bevy can run headless -- MinimalPlugins, or
     RenderPlugin configured with no backend -- if what you are asserting is
     scene/document structure rather than pixels. Your four `proof::*` tests
     already passed without one, which suggests most of your evidence does not
     need a device at all.
  2. Keep the device test but make it SKIP on a host without a real adapter,
     explicitly and loudly. The risk is the modelled-authored-unreachable shape
     this repo keeps rediscovering: a test that never runs anywhere is not
     coverage, so if you do this, say where it DOES run and how often.
  3. Treat the segfault as the finding and chase it -- llvmpipe + this wgpu is
     a known-rough combination, and Mesa 22.3.6 is old. This is the most
     expensive option and the one least likely to stay fixed.

outboard and gate all rc=0, and the fixture race you lost twice is won. This is
the last thing between you and main.
